world.title: ‘Absolutely no ambiguity: Pakistan says Mecca pact applies as Saudi Arabia faces Houthi drone threat
world.summary: Pakistan reaffirmed its commitment to the defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Thursday, emphasizing the clarity of the Mecca pact. This statement comes amid rising tensions in the Gulf region, particularly in light of recent threats from Houthi drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia. The Pakistani defence minister, Khwaja Asif, underscored the importance of this alliance.

world.title: Poland's Tusk says Russia plans 'hybrid' missile and drone attacks on Kyiv's allies
world.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated on Thursday that intelligence agencies indicate Russia is planning 'hybrid' drone and missile attacks targeting nations that support Ukraine. Tusk's comments highlight concerns about escalating threats from Russia amid ongoing tensions. The warning underscores the potential risks faced by countries aiding Ukraine in the conflict, emphasizing the need for vigilance and preparedness.

world.title: EU Commission proposes under-13s social media ban
world.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced a proposal to enhance online safety for children on September 17. The plan includes a ban on social media access for individuals under 13 years old and mandates that online services create secure accounts specifically designed for children. This initiative aims to protect young users from various online dangers.

business.title: How a 27-year-old math geek at Anthropic made the world afraid of AI
business.summary: Jacob Coxon, a 27-year-old former employee at Anthropic, recently announced his resignation on X, quickly gaining significant attention. His posts garnered over 170 million views within days, making him a prominent voice in discussions about AI risks. While not the first to raise concerns this year, his influence has amplified fears surrounding artificial intelligence.

business.title: Tata Sons board-room battle: Stalemate allowed chairman to vote on his own reappointment
business.summary: Tata Sons faced a boardroom battle over chairman reappointment, allowing him to vote on his own position amid a stalemate. The Noel Tata camp relied on Article 121A, requiring majority approval from Tata Trusts' nominees for certain votes. With only two nominees present, the situation highlighted divisions within the company, raising questions about governance and decision-making processes.

business.title: Goldman's October hike call underscores renewed Fed tightening risks
business.summary: Goldman Sachs anticipates the US Federal Reserve will implement another interest rate hike in October. This expectation follows recent signals from policymakers indicating a need for further tightening to achieve inflation targets. The potential increase comes after the central bank's initial rate hike in three years, highlighting ongoing concerns about inflation and the Fed's monetary policy direction.

technology.title: Artificial intelligence now beats some of the best human forecasters
technology.summary: Artificial intelligence has surpassed some top human forecasters, particularly in complex prediction tasks. Unlike traditional models that focus on specific data, AI systems, such as those used on Metaculus, utilize large language models (LLMs) to analyze diverse information. This advancement marks a significant shift in forecasting capabilities, moving beyond conventional methods to enhance prediction accuracy across various domains.

technology.title: Oppo's ColorOS 17 goes official, check the latest features and rollout schedule here
technology.summary: Oppo has officially launched ColorOS 17 at its developer conference in China, introducing new AI features and performance enhancements. The update aims to improve user experience with various significant changes. Additionally, Oppo provided a detailed rollout schedule for the new operating system, ensuring users are informed about when they can expect to receive the update on their devices.

technology.title: Your Galaxy S25 One UI 9 upgrade is closer than you think
technology.summary: Samsung has announced that the Galaxy S25 series will soon receive the One UI 9 upgrade, alleviating user anticipation. This upgrade is expected to roll out earlier than many anticipated, despite other devices gaining access to the new operating system ahead of the S25. Users can look forward to enhanced features and improvements in the upcoming update.

sports.title: Kylian Mbappe praises Lamine Yamal amidst Ballon d’Or battle: ‘Very talented player’
sports.summary: Kylian Mbappe recently praised Lamine Yamal, calling him a "very talented player," amid the ongoing Ballon d'Or discussions. The conversation has shifted significantly over the past week, narrowing down to Mbappe and Yamal as leading contenders. Despite this focus, other players remain in contention for the prestigious award, highlighting the competitive nature of this year's race.

sports.title: Tavengwa Mukuhlani appointed ICC's deputy chairperson
sports.summary: Tavengwa Mukuhlani, Chairman of Zimbabwe Cricket, has been appointed Deputy Chairperson of the International Cricket Council (ICC), effective immediately. The ICC announced his appointment on Thursday, with his term set to last until November 2027. Mukuhlani succeeds Imran Khwaja, who recently departed from the Board after nearly two decades as an Associate director.

sports.title: Mohammad Rizwan’s troubles deepen as Lahore HC dismisses petition in online betting, gambling probe
sports.summary: Lahore High Court dismissed Mohammad Rizwan's petition related to an online betting and gambling investigation. Rizwan challenged the National Crime Control and Investigation Agency's summons, claiming lack of jurisdiction and insufficient reasoning for questioning. The Pakistan Cricket Board is currently awaiting forensic findings before determining any disciplinary actions against him in connection with the ongoing cyber crime case.

health.title: Bangladesh Measles Outbreak: WHO & Unicef Warning
health.summary: Bangladesh is facing a severe measles outbreak, with over 1,000 child fatalities reported. Authorities are implementing one of the country's largest emergency immunization campaigns to combat the crisis. Since March 2026, more than 194,000 individuals have been infected. The World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF are closely monitoring the situation as efforts to contain the outbreak continue.

health.title: New Study Says Your Sleep Score Might Be Overly Optimistic
health.summary: A new study reveals that sleep trackers may provide overly optimistic sleep scores compared to clinical lab tests. Researchers compared data from wearable devices with gold-standard sleep assessments, highlighting discrepancies in sleep quality and duration measurements. The findings suggest that individuals relying on trackers for sleep insights may not receive an accurate representation of their actual sleep patterns and health.

health.title: When memory files get mixed up
health.summary: Research from Binghamton University indicates that aging affects the hippocampus's ability to manage memory storage and retrieval. While older individuals may experience forgetfulness, memories do not vanish entirely; instead, they become less precise. The findings, published in the journal Cerebral Cortex, highlight the complexities of memory processing in the aging brain, suggesting alterations rather than complete loss.

science.title: Did starfish begin in China? A 518-million-year-old fossil may rewrite their origin story
science.summary: A 518-million-year-old fossil discovered in China may alter the understanding of starfish evolution. The tiny creature, which used tentacles for feeding instead of relying on gills, suggests a more active feeding strategy in early echinoderms. This finding could provide new insights into the evolutionary history of starfish and their relatives, challenging previous assumptions about their origins.

science.title: Quote of the day by Stephen Hawking: "We are just an advanced breed of monkeys on a minor planet of…"
science.summary: Stephen Hawking's quote reflects on humanity's achievements, including space exploration and technological advancements. Despite these milestones, he emphasizes our insignificance in the vast universe. Hawking's perspective invites contemplation on the human condition, highlighting that while we have made remarkable progress, we remain a minor species on a small planet within an expansive cosmos, underscoring our limited place in the universe.

science.title: T. Rex had a 36°C body temperature? UCLA scientists reveal the dinosaur’s heat for the first time
science.summary: Scientists have measured the body temperature of Tyrannosaurus rex for the first time, estimating it to be around 36°C. This finding is notably similar to human body temperature. For over 60 million years, T. rex has been understood primarily through fossils, but this research provides new insights into its physiology and potential metabolic processes.

entertainment.title: BREAKING: Akshay Kumar and Vipul Shah’s Samuk takes authenticity to another level in London; makers use REAL helicopter for dramatic sequence instead of VFX
entertainment.summary: Akshay Kumar is filming the sci-fi survival thriller "Samuk," directed by Vipul Amrutlal Shah, in London. The production team is prioritizing authenticity, opting to use a real helicopter for a dramatic sequence instead of relying on visual effects. This decision reflects their commitment to creating a realistic portrayal of the film's world, enhancing the overall cinematic experience.

entertainment.title: Prithvi Shaw, girlfriend Akriti Agarwal part ways months after engagement
entertainment.summary: Indian cricketer Prithvi Shaw and his fiancée Akriti Agarwal have mutually decided to end their engagement six months after its announcement. Agarwal stated that differing future goals and circumstances led to the separation. She requested privacy during this time and urged the public not to speculate about the reasons behind their decision to part ways.

entertainment.title: Horoscope Tomorrow, September 18, 2026: Fresh opportunities may emerge as you move beyond old challenges
entertainment.summary: On September 18, 2026, horoscopes suggest that fresh opportunities may arise as individuals confront past challenges. A significant decision or situation may require a factual approach rather than emotional reactions. Clarity may emerge regarding unresolved issues, and conversations or agreements could lead to closure. Overall, the day encourages reflection and rational decision-making for all sun signs.
